items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: Good drummer. Bob Aang, Johnny, Great Happy, Black Happy.

ctx.x: Well, I ask him who some good drummers were in all this.

So who was some good drummers in them days? Good drummer. Bob Aang, Johnny, Great Happy, Black Happy. Let me see who else. Facial, you remember Facial? Yeah. Bo I don't know who's writing again. Faso, that's all I know.
Eddie Woods. Eddie Woods? Eddie Woods is Faso's name.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: I said, how do you, Black Happy? Black Happy said 41.

ctx.x: What band was that? Let me see my band. Oh, that was a little bit of a band. Bobby used to play. And we had facial for it. And with facial and that, we got Bobby. And when Bobby left, we got Black Benny. And that's where Black Benny said he was going to make a man out of himself. And Black Benny stuck with it, so they got killed. And a little while after that, that's where the band broke up. Maurice come in, you know, from the war. Chris Johnson had taken all the Cornette players. We had to keep on changing…
Ask me about bazooka players. Bazooka? Yeah, you know, like those big horns made out of two pieces of pipe.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: And, uh, that Maurice. And Black Happy.

ctx.x: Ask him who was in Octaves' band.

I don't know whether he did it in Redding Joe. He said, who was in Octaves' band? Who was in Octaves' band? Who was in Octaves' band? Walsh, he got Walsh. The sacrifice man. The big brother. Edmund Washington. Yeah, yeah. And, uh, that Maurice. And Black Happy. And, uh, no, Bottler. They got rid of Bottler and got, uh, got washed, you see.
Ask him what Bottler's name was.
